claims.statement: Game data from DofusDB, including quest-giver and objective NPCs, subareas, achievements, achievement categories and dungeons with their bosses, is read-only in the panel except each record's Corrección de Torre and refreshed by pnpm data:refresh, and Torre picks it through relationship fields.

The DofusDB client pages collections in pages of 50 until the reported total or an empty page, optionally restricting each row to selected fields with $select[] parameters, and fetches records by ID deduplicated in chunks of 40 using id[$in][] filters.

The DofusDB client waits 50 ms between requests, sends the User-Agent ta-web/datos-del-juego, gives each request a 30-second timeout, and accepts injected fetch, sleep, log and random so tests never reach the network.

fetchQuestData loads every DofusDB quest, fetches by ID only the NPCs named in start positions and objectives and the maps of start positions, and downloads every sub-area, area, dungeon, achievement, achievement category, the whole item catalog and the whole monster catalog with fetchAll, selecting only the fields used.

mapQuest names a quest in Spanish, falling back to French and then to 'Misión <id>', keeps the raw startCriterion, and builds start positions with NPC names and map coordinates, leaving nulls when a lookup is missing instead of failing.

Quest prerequisites are only the Qf=<id> terms joined by & in startCriterion; a level containing | is treated as alternatives and contributes none, other terms such as Qa= are ignored, and the result is deduplicated and excludes the quest itself.

DofusDB's need.quests is not used for prerequisites because it lists every quest mentioned in the criterion: quest 275 lists 272, 273 and 274 for (Qf=272|Qf=273|Qf=274) and gets no prerequisites, and quest 879 lists 871 and 878 for Qf=871&Qa=878 and gets only 871.

refreshQuests writes quests through the local API with overrideAccess true in two passes: first creating or updating quest fields by dofusId only when they differ, then linking prerequisites by Payload ID and skipping and counting missing ones.

A refresh with unchanged data writes nothing, refreshedAt is set only on rows created or changed in that run, nothing is ever deleted, and the function returns created, updated, unchanged and failed counts for quests, items, monsters and dungeons plus missing prerequisite, item, monster and boss counts.

pnpm data:refresh runs scripts/refresh-game-data.ts with payload run; the script starts Payload with getPayload, writes to the DATABASE_URL database or the pnpm db:dev one when it is empty, prints the run's report, and exits with code 1 when the refresh failed or left failed rows because payload run otherwise exits 0.

A full refresh downloads about 2,000 quests, the whole monster catalog of about 5,000 and the whole item catalog of about 21,500 items from DofusDB, and a rerun changes only what DofusDB changed without deleting rows.
Payload schema push runs only under next dev, so other processes rely on applied migrations.
Agent access rules grant full access to dev and read access to prod; prod writes, including database changes, go through release.yml or need Daniel's explicit yes for that one action.
Nothing loads from DofusDB or Ankama at runtime; item icons and monster images are imported once into Media by the refresh and served from there.

mapItem and mapMonster name rows in Spanish with a French fallback and then 'Objeto <id>' or 'Monstruo <id>', keep an item's level, typeId and iconId plus its superTypeId from type.superTypeId, and store a monster's gfxId as iconId along with its grade levels, boss and archmonster flags and first subarea.

questRewards computes rewards for a level-200 character from each step's untiered entries plus the entry of the tier holding the level (the last tier when none does), using fixe(L) = L(100+2L)^2/20 x duration x experienceRatio and XP = 0.3 fixe(lower) + 0.7 fixe(upper) with lower = min(level, optimum) and upper capped at 1.5 times lower, and kamas = (K^2 + 20K - 20) x kamasRatio x duration with K the optimum or, when the entry scales with the player, min(level, optimum).
Reward XP and kamas are floored per step before summing, so quest 241 yields 5,679,336 XP rather than the 5,679,337 a single final floor would give.
Quest 1977 yields 24,316 XP and 552 kamas, matching Torre's guide and dofusdb.fr.
Reward items are summed by item across steps, and emote, spell, title and job reward IDs are collected without duplicates as plain DofusDB IDs.

questNeeds takes delivered and shown items from BringItemToNpc objectives, monsters from FightMonster, MultiFightMonster, FightMonstersOnMap and BringSoulToNpc objectives, sets walksMaps for DiscoverMap and DiscoverSubArea objectives, and ignores FreeForm, GoToNpc, CraftItem and other objectives.

Because DofusDB's need.items summary already includes delivered items, questNeeds keeps the larger of the need.items and delivered quantities instead of their sum, so quest 245 needs 2 of item 8993, not 3.

A quest guide's Necesitás item list is copied from the linked quest's computed needs.items without quest items of supertype 14, while Torre's editorial Necesitás text stays in the guide's summary.needs.notes, which the fill never touches.

Before the quests, refreshQuests creates or updates items, then monsters, then dungeons by dofusId only when they change, and resolves reward and need references to their Payload IDs, dropping and counting references with no stored row.

mapWithConcurrency returns results in input order, runs at most limit calls at once, starts nothing new after the first error and rejects with that error once running calls settle, and throws a RangeError for a limit that is not an integer of at least 1.

Within each step (items, monsters, dungeons, the quests' first pass and the prerequisites pass) refreshQuests writes rows concurrently with mapWithConcurrency, keeping the steps in the same order, with options.concurrency defaulting to DEFAULT_WRITE_CONCURRENCY, which is 8.
refreshQuests sums its created, updated, unchanged and missing counts from the result each write returns rather than from shared counters.
The refresh source notes that writing rows one at a time took about half an hour against Neon because each write is several round trips to the database.
writeConcurrencyFromEnv returns 8 when DOFUSDB_WRITE_CONCURRENCY is empty or unset and throws on any value that is not an integer of at least 1.
Each concurrent write holds one Postgres pool connection; the pool sets no explicit max, so pg's default of 10 applies, and .env.example advises not going above 9.

scripts/refresh-game-data.ts reads DOFUSDB_WRITE_CONCURRENCY and its --schedule option before starting Payload, prints a busy message and exits cleanly when another refresh is running, and prints the total time and the run's report.
An integration test runs the refresh over both fixtures with concurrency 1 and then with concurrency 8 and expects equal counts and equal stored data, comparing relationships by DofusDB ID.
The DofusDB client retries network errors and HTTP 429, 502, 503 and 504 up to 4 times, waiting 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 seconds each plus up to 25% random jitter, and does not retry any other non-2xx status.
On a 429 the client waits for the Retry-After header, read as seconds or an HTTP date and capped at 60 seconds, falling back to the computed backoff when the header is missing or unreadable.

When retries run out or a status is not retryable, the client throws a Spanish error naming the URL and the number of attempts, keeping the network error as its cause, and its optional log callback receives one line per retry.
refreshGameData creates the DofusDB client with its run log, so pnpm data:refresh prints a line for each retry.
While writing catalog rows, refreshCatalog logs progress every 2,000 saved rows because the item catalog exceeds 20,000 rows.

A quest guide's summary is copied from the linked quest's prerequisites and PL> level, rewards and first start position, and later refreshes do not change existing guides because only empty guide fields are filled, and only on create or quest change.

requiredTerms in src/lib/dofusdb/criterion.ts returns the criterion terms joined by & at the top level or inside &-only brackets, in order, returns nothing for a level containing |, and returns an empty list for a missing or empty criterion; mapQuest prerequisites and the guide's requiredLevel both use it.

mapQuest stores the zone as the Spanish name of the area of the first start map whose sub-area and area are known, and the achievement whose need.quests lists the quest with the quest's position and the list's total, taking the lowest achievement ID when several list it.
questRewards also computes experienceMin, the XP at each step's optimal level capped at 200, floored per step and summed, which is the start of the XP range the guide shows.

refreshNpcs imports each NPC's right- and left-facing renders into media once, keyed by NPC, direction and a hash of the look in gameAsset, reusing a matching media document before downloading, and keeps the previous render when the download fails.
Renders are fetched from renderer.dofusdb.fr with the look hex-encoded, trimmed of transparent margin and capped at 720 pixels high before upload, and renders of an earlier look stay in media.
refreshGameData runs refreshNpcs after refreshQuests, refreshSubAreas and refreshAchievements, and counts NPCs and their renders imported, reused or missing in the summary.
The achievement select includes objectiveIds and rewardIds because without them DofusDB does not attach each achievement's objectives and rewards.

After the quests, refreshGameData runs refreshSubAreas, refreshAchievements, refreshNpcs, then ensureAchievementPages (after NPCs because the default representative is an NPC), then imports the game images of the items and monsters some page shows, and the script finally prints the dungeon report.

refreshGameImages imports each item or monster image once into media keyed by dofusdb-<kind>-image:<id>, skips rows already linked to that key, reuses a matching media document before downloading the 128 px PNG from api.dofusdb.fr, and links nothing when DofusDB fails so the next refresh retries.

gameImageTargets collects items from quest rewards (level tiers included) and needs, achievement rewards, achievement page rewards and guide needs lists, reward items and level tiers, and monsters from quest needs, guide fight blocks, metalogro representatives and every dungeon boss, drafts included.

refreshAchievements upserts every achievement category and the achievements under Misiones and Eventos, imports their icons once, skips and counts missing quests and items, writes only changes and never deletes.
fetchWhere returns only the first page of 50 rows matching a Feathers query with URL-encoded values and optional $select[] fields; it is meant for searching, not for walking a collection.

questStages keeps each quest's stages and objectives in DofusDB order, classifies objectives as free, npc, bring, show, fight, map or craft with the parameters each names, stores DofusDB's 0 as null, and reorders the two Silvestre stages the old checklist did differently.
objectiveNpcIds collects the NPCs an objective names in its class parameter and in {npc,id} markers in its text, without duplicates or 0.
refreshSubAreas creates or updates every sub-area by dofusId with its Spanish name and area, only when they change, and never deletes one.
mapDungeon names a dungeon in Spanish with a Mazmorra <id> fallback, keeps its optimal player level, and links its bosses to stored monsters, counting bosses missing from the monsters collection.

dungeonNoteReport classifies the dungeon notes of published achievement pages, Dofus guides and quest guides through the same functions as each page, so a boss without an image counts as generic, and records how each note matched; the printed report groups each note once with its pages by name, by boss, by hand or unmatched.
The monster select adds isBoss, isMiniBoss, subareas and only the grade levels, and the dungeon select adds optimalPlayerLevel, because the souls checklist needs them.

pnpm data:dungeon-notes prints only the dungeon report without downloading from DofusDB or writing, running through runPayloadScript, which exits with 1 when starting Payload, the task or shutting Payload down fails.

startGameDataRefresh closes runs stuck as running for more than two hours, creates the run row with a unique lock so a second refresh from any process returns busy, and resolves done with the row closed as ok, partial when rows failed, or failed with the error, never rejecting.
The refresh run's trigger is schedule with --schedule, script without options, or panel from the endpoint, and triggerFromArgs rejects any other option.
rowGuard counts a row that fails to save, logs only the first failures, and stops the refresh when more than MAX_ROW_FAILURES (20) rows of one collection fail.

summaryLines gives one line per game data collection with created, updated, unchanged and failed rows, then the image counts, the new pages and the skipped references, and rowFailures counts failed rows without missing images.

questNeeds treats a show objective as not spending its item: it removes the part DofusDB generated for it from need.items and counts the item as the larger of what is given and the largest single show.

levelRewards splits a quest's rewards into level tiers at every tier boundary up to 200, computes each tier's totals at its highest level, merges consecutive tiers that give the same items, and gives no tiers when fewer than two remain.
refreshGameData writes without a user, so the Torre correction of each game data record stays as it was, and an integration test checks a DofusDB change never touches it or what Torre wrote.
